meanings.en: to be glad, pleased, or happy to see someone
meanings.note: Commonly used in greetings such as 반갑습니다 or 반가워요.

examples.trans: Nice to meet you.
I was really glad to see my friend after a long time.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: The division at a television network that produces variety and entertainment shows.

examples.trans: He works in the network's variety department.
The new PDs of the variety department gathered in the lobby.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: first, before others, ahead of time
meanings.note: Indicates priority in order or time.

examples.trans: It's late, so I'll head in first.
Who arrived first?

meanings.note: Often seen on Korean restaurant signs to claim status as the original establishment.

examples.trans: This restaurant is the original one in this alley.
That singer is called the original idol.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response or acknowledgment.

examples.trans: Yes, I understand.
Yes, I'll go right now.

meanings.note: Functions as both a noun and a temporal adverb.

examples.trans: The weather is really nice today.
There are two meetings today.

meanings.note: Refers to planned events or work tasks for a day or period.

examples.trans: What is your schedule like this week?
The filming schedule changed suddenly.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem adjective: 바쁘다 + -아요 becomes 바빠요.

examples.trans: Work at the company is so busy these days.
If you're busy, please contact me later.

meanings.note: Short for 연예 오락; used for television variety programs.

examples.trans: On weekends I watch variety shows with my family.
That actor is also very popular on variety shows.

meanings.note: Interrogative or indefinite pronoun; often shortened to 뭐 in casual speech.

examples.trans: What is your favorite food?
What can I help you with?

meanings.note: Counted with the counter 권.

examples.text: 서점에서 새 책을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.trans: I bought a new book at the bookstore.
This book is good for beginners to read.

meanings.note: Indicates existence or location of people or things.
Used with -이/가 to express possession.

examples.trans: There is coffee on the desk.
Do you have time tomorrow afternoon?

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Paired with 보다 ('to take an exam') or 준비하다 ('to prepare for an exam').

examples.trans: There is a Korean exam next week.
I studied hard to prepare for the exam.

meanings.note: Transitive verb taking -을/를.

examples.trans: I prepared the presentation materials in advance.
The time spent preparing for a trip is also enjoyable.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Past tense is 샀다 / 샀어요.

examples.trans: I bought fruit at the mart.
I need to buy a birthday present for my friend.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used when speaking politely to seniors or strangers.

examples.trans: I am a new employee who joined this year.
I have read that book too.

meanings.note: Follows a noun to exclude it; with -도 (말고도) it means 'besides' or 'apart from'.

examples.trans: Please give me tea instead of coffee.

examples.text: 나 말고도 그 사실을 아는 사람이 많다.
examples.trans: Besides me, there are many people who know that fact.

meanings.note: Determiner modifying a following noun.

examples.text: 그런 실수는 누구나 할 수 있어요.
examples.trans: Anyone can make a mistake like that.
This is the first time I'm hearing a story like that.

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent is 성함.

examples.trans: Please write your name here.
What is that puppy's name?

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.

meanings.en: returning purchased goods for a refund
meanings.note: Paired with 하다 to mean 'to return a purchase'.

examples.trans: The size didn't fit, so I returned it.
You must have the receipt to make a return.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Combines with many nouns (such as 반품하다, 준비하다) to form verbs.

examples.trans: What do you usually do on weekends?
I finished doing my homework.

meanings.en: next, the following time or order
meanings.note: With -에 (다음에), means 'next time' or 'later'.

examples.trans: Let's meet again next time.
We have to get off at the next station.

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Also used in farewells like 다음에 봐요 ('See you next time').

examples.trans: I watched a movie with a friend on the weekend.
See you at the office tomorrow!
